requirement: The Controller of Certifying Authorities must maintain a public database containing the disclosure record of every Certifying Authority.
The Controller of Certifying Authorities must publish notice of suspension or revocation of a Certifying Authority in the database maintained by him.
Public authorities must disseminate information in an accessible format, including electronic formats, at a cost-effective manner.
Public authorities must appoint Assistant Public Information Officers to receive and forward information requests and appeals promptly.
Public authorities must extend the response period by five days when information requests or appeals are submitted to Assistant Public Information Officers.
Public authorities must deal with information requests and provide reasonable assistance to information seekers.
Public authorities must provide requested information within thirty days of receipt, unless exempted.
Failure to respond within the specified period is deemed a refusal of the request.
The Information Officer must inform the applicant of the reasons for rejecting a request for information, including any findings on material questions of fact and the basis for those findings.
The Public Information Officer must provide a written notice to the third party within five days of receiving a request for information that has been treated as confidential by the third party.
The Public Information Officer must invite the third party to submit a written or oral representation regarding the disclosure of confidential information.

The Public Information Officer must provide the third party with an opportunity to make a representation against the proposed disclosure of confidential information within ten days of receiving the notice.
The Public Information Officer must make a decision on the disclosure of confidential information within forty days of receiving the request, after considering the third party's representation.
The Public Information Officer must include a statement in the notice that the third party has the right to appeal the decision regarding the disclosure of confidential information.
The Central Information Commission or State Information Commission must impose a penalty of up to twenty-five thousand rupees for unjustified refusals or malafidely denied requests for information.
Public authorities must provide the postal and street address, phone and fax number, and electronic mail address of their Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer.
Public authorities must specify the manner and form in which requests for access to information shall be made to their Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer.
Public authorities must specify the assistance available from and the duties of their Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer under the RTI Act.
A Certifying Authority must comply with conditions and restrictions specified by regulations to maintain recognition under the IT Act 2000.
A Certifying Authority must maintain compliance with the conditions and restrictions to avoid revocation of recognition.
A Certifying Authority must obtain prior approval from the Central Government before being recognized under the IT Act 2000.
A Certifying Authority must issue valid electronic signature certificates that are recognized under the IT Act 2000.
A Certifying Authority's licence may not be suspended or revoked without providing a reasonable opportunity to show cause against the proposed action.
A Certifying Authority whose licence has been suspended may not issue any electronic signature Certificate during the suspension.
Certifying Authorities must ensure that all employees and engaged personnel comply with the provisions of the IT Act, 2000, rules, regulations, and orders made thereunder.
Certifying Authorities must display their licence at a conspicuous place of their premises.
Certifying Authorities must surrender their licence immediately upon suspension or revocation.
Certifying Authorities must disclose, in the manner specified by regulations, notice of the revocation or suspension of their Certifying Authority certificate.
Certifying Authority must communicate suspension of a Digital Signature Certificate to the subscriber.
Certifying Authority may revoke a Digital Signature Certificate under specified conditions.
Certifying Authority must not reject an application unless the applicant is given a reasonable opportunity to show cause against the proposed rejection.
Certifying Authority must issue a Digital Signature Certificate upon application, subject to prescribed conditions.
Certifying Authority must charge a fee not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees for the issuance of a Digital Signature Certificate.
Certifying Authority must issue a certification practice statement or a statement containing specified particulars with the application for a Digital Signature Certificate.
Certifying Authority must certify that the Digital Signature Certificate is issued in accordance with prescribed conditions.

Certifying Authority must take action if any event occurs that may materially and adversely affect the integrity of its computer system or the conditions subject to which a Digital Signature Certificate was granted.
Certifying Authorities must revoke a Digital Signature Certificate if their private key or security system is compromised in a manner materially affecting the certificate's reliability.
Certifying Authorities must communicate the revocation of a Digital Signature Certificate to the subscriber.
Certifying Authorities must publish notices of suspension or revocation in the repository specified in the Digital Signature Certificate.
Certifying Authorities must publish notices of suspension or revocation in all specified repositories.
Subscribers must generate a key pair by applying the security procedure specified by the Certifying Authority.
Subscribers must ensure all representations made to the Certifying Authority are true and accurate.
A subscriber must promptly notify the Certifying Authority if the private key corresponding to their Digital Signature Certificate has been compromised.
Intermediaries must furnish documents, returns, or reports to the Controller or Certifying Authority as required.
Intermediaries must maintain records of Certifying Authority disclosures as specified in section 18(1)(n) of the IT Act 2000.
Intermediaries must specify conditions and restrictions for recognizing foreign Certifying Authorities under section 19(1) of the IT Act 2000.
Intermediaries must observe other standards set for Certifying Authorities under section 30(d) of the IT Act 2000.
Intermediaries must specify the manner of disclosure by Certifying Authorities under section 34(1) of the IT Act 2000.
Intermediaries must specify the manner of communication of private key compromise to Certifying Authorities under section 42(2) of the IT Act 2000.
Public authorities must designate a Public Information Officer within one hundred days of the enactment of the RTI Act.
An appeal against a decision of the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer must be filed within the time specified in sub-section (3) of section 7.
Certifying Authorities must follow specific procedures when issuing electronic signature certificates.
Certifying Authorities must ensure compliance with the IT Act and related regulations.
Certifying Authorities must specify the conditions under which they conduct their business.
Certifying Authorities must specify the manner in which they shall conduct their dealings with subscribers.
Applications for Certifying Authority licenses must include a certification practice statement.
Applications for Certifying Authority licenses must include a statement on procedures for identifying the applicant.

Certifying authorities must use reasonable efforts to notify any person who is likely to be affected by an occurrence that materially and adversely affects the reliability of a certificate or the Authority's ability to perform its services.

Certifying authorities must act in accordance with the procedure specified in their certification practice statement to deal with events or situations that materially and adversely affect the reliability of a certificate or the Authority's ability to perform its services.
Certifying authorities must provide a certification practice statement relevant to their operations.
Certifying authorities must ensure that their services provide a reasonable level of reliability suited to the intended functions.
